title: Done isn’t the same as right.
narration: An AI can finish a task and still deliver the wrong thing. What matters is whether the result matches what you agreed to.

title: One room. A shared job.
narration: Meet PromiseKeeper. One Switch room brings you, a coordinator, and a builder together. You confirm the request. The agents do the work and check the result.

title: Two columns. Three orders.
narration: Here’s the request: export three sample orders with order number and total only. The coordinator confirms the details before the builder starts.

title: Extra fields. Caught.
narration: For this demo, we start with a deliberately flawed export. It includes email and internal notes. The program runs, but the check catches those extra columns.

title: A real handoff. A corrected file.
narration: The coordinator sends the failure back through Switch. The builder fixes the exporter and generates a new file. The same checks now pass.

title: You approve this version.
narration: You inspect the file and approve that checked version. Its receipt connects your review to the exact file. In this prototype, review happens through a local command.

title: New request. Fresh review.
narration: Now add email to the request. PromiseKeeper records a new version and clears the old approval. The changed request needs a fresh check and review.

title: Keep the request, work and review connected.
narration: That’s PromiseKeeper: a shared task with a verifiable result. Real agent handoffs through Switch, a human review step, and nine passing tests. A changed request never inherits an old approval.
